purpose: Per-row conformance breadth contract for docs/PYTHON_STANDARDS.md, introduced by issue #593 (Part 1 of #248). Each entry records the semantic categories a green row's registered evidence actually proves against the pinned CPython oracle, and the categories that are known-unsupported or intentionally deviating. Validated by scripts/check_conformance_breadth.py. Recording a gap here does not change the row's status; correcting statuses is Part 2 (#594).

proven.category: true division `/` on float operands
floor division `//` on int operands

not_proven.category: `/` on two int operands yielding a float
not_proven.reason: The fixture divides floats only, so the PEP's headline change -- int/int no longer truncating -- is never exercised by this row's evidence.

not_proven.category: `__truediv__`/`__floordiv__` operator overloading
not_proven.reason: Operator dunder dispatch on user-defined classes is outside the scalar numeric surface this fixture covers.

proven.category: `Optional[int]` (`T | None`, either operand order) declared, assigned, and read back with an `is`/`is not None` presence test, module-global and function-local
a function returning `int | None` from both branches (a real value and `None`), with the caller reading the result's presence

flow-sensitive narrowing of an `Optional[int]` back to plain `int` inside a top-level `if name is not None:`/`if name is None: ... else:` branch, module-global and function-local, including kill-on-reassignment inside the narrowed branch and the early-return continuation shape (`if name is None: ...; return` narrowing every read after the `if`)

`Optional[float]`/`Optional[bool]` (`T | None`, either operand order) declared, assigned, and read back with an `is`/`is not None` presence test, module-global and function-local, including truthiness and a function returning `float | None`/`bool | None` from both branches

flow-sensitive narrowing of an `Optional[float]`/`Optional[bool]` back to plain `float`/`bool` inside a top-level `if name is not None:`/`if name is None: ... else:` branch, the same mechanism proven above for `Optional[int]` (never `Ty::Int`-specific in its own implementation, confirmed by #809/D-204)

not_proven.category: a general union with neither side `None`, or any 3+-operand union chain
not_proven.reason: rejected pre-lowering with T0048; not implemented -- only the exact `T | None`/`None | T` 2-operand shape is recognized (D-197, #763, Part 1 of #747).

not_proven.category: `Optional[T]` for any `T` outside `{int, float, bool}`
not_proven.reason: rejected with T0049; codegen's `{ inner, present }` representation is exercised and tested for `Optional[int]`/`Optional[float]`/`Optional[bool]` only (widened from `Optional[int]`-only by #809, D-204, Part 3 of #747) -- `Optional[str]` and other refcounted/pointer inner types, and general containers, remain out of scope, mirroring the `list[int]`-only (T0034) and `dict[str, int]`-only (T0036) v0.2 scope cuts.

not_proven.category: narrowing through a compound `and`/`or` test (e.g. `if x is not None and y is not None:`), or through a non-top-level test embedded in a larger boolean expression
not_proven.reason: only a bare top-level `name is None`/`name is not None` test is recognized (`pycc_hir::optional_none_test`); not implemented (D-204, #769, Part 2 of #747).

not_proven.category: narrowing a name to `None` (the mirror of the implemented shape: `if name is not None: ... else: <use name as None>`, or a `return`-terminated `if name is not None:` guard narrowing the continuation to `None`)
not_proven.reason: deliberately not implemented -- there is no `Ty::None`-typed narrowing target in this design (D-204, #769, Part 2 of #747).

not_proven.category: `raise` (instead of `return`) as a branch terminator for the early-return continuation shape
not_proven.reason: `definitely_terminates` (`pycc_hir::definitely_terminates`) deliberately does not treat `raise` as a terminator; only a bare `return`, or an exhaustive nested `if`/`else` both ending in `return`, count (D-204, #769, Part 2 of #747).

proven.category: `print()` called as a function with multiple positional arguments

not_proven.category: `sep=` and `end=` keyword arguments
not_proven.reason: Keyword call arguments are rejected with C0001 at crates/pycc_hir/src/expr.rs:399: Parts 1 and 2 of #884 bind keywords and fill defaults only for a call to a module-level `def`, and `print` is a builtin, so PEP 3105's function signature -- the substance of turning `print` into a function -- is unreachable.

not_proven.category: `file=` and `flush=` keyword arguments
not_proven.reason: Same C0001 rejection of keyword call arguments at crates/pycc_hir/src/expr.rs:399.

proven.category: parameter annotations on a function definition
a return annotation on a function definition

not_proven.category: `__annotations__` introspection at runtime
not_proven.reason: pycc consumes annotations at compile time and exposes no runtime annotation mapping; PEP 3107's introspection half has no execution path.

proven.category: `try`/`except` selecting the handler matching the raised exception type, across several handlers on one `try`
`else` running exactly when the `try` body completes without raising
`finally` running on both the normal and the exceptional path, in CPython's own ordering relative to the handler body
bare `raise` re-raising the active exception out of a handler to an enclosing `try`
an exception propagating across a function-call boundary to a caller's handler
user-defined exception classes derived from `Exception`: raising them, catching them by their own name, and catching a subclass through a base-class or `Exception` handler

not_proven.category: `except ValueError as exc:` binding the caught exception to a name, and reading its payload
not_proven.reason: pycc does not materialize an exception object a handler can bind yet; handler selection is by type alone. Tracked by #382's remaining cluster.

not_proven.category: a user-defined exception class that declares its own `__init__`, and the instance state such a constructor would carry
not_proven.reason: pycc raises and catches by runtime type tag; the message string is the only payload the exception object carries, so a class with its own constructor is rejected with `C0001`. Tracked by #703.

not_proven.category: `except*` and `ExceptionGroup` (PEP 654)
not_proven.reason: A separate PEP with its own matrix row; tracked by #542, not by this row.

not_proven.category: traceback rendering for an uncaught exception
not_proven.reason: #707 gave pycc a single raise-site frame (the enclosing function's name, `"<module>"` at top level) rendered as a `Traceback (most recent call last):` block, but it carries no source file name or line number -- HIR drops the source span before `pycc_mir` ever sees a `raise` statement, so there is nothing to render one from. This repository's conformance oracle (`tests/conformance.rs`) also only diffs the *successful*-exit stdout of matching runs, never the stderr of a program that exits 1, so an uncaught exception's text has no automated CPython comparison regardless of format. Neither gap is tracked by #606, which is exclusively about implicit `__context__` chaining (misciting it here predated #707); a source-span/line-number row would need its own new issue if pursued.

proven.category: `ABC` base class with an `@abstractmethod`
concrete subclasses overriding the abstract method
`super().__init__()` delegation from a subclass

not_proven.category: instantiating an abstract class raising `TypeError`
not_proven.reason: The fixture instantiates only concrete subclasses, so the PEP's central enforcement behavior is not compared against the oracle.

not_proven.category: `register()` virtual subclasses and `__subclasshook__`
not_proven.reason: The isinstance-hook half of PEP 3119 is not exercised by this fixture.

proven.category: a class decorator applied with `@` syntax (`@dataclass`)

not_proven.category: a user-defined class decorator
not_proven.reason: The fixture uses only the stdlib `@dataclass`, which pycc recognizes as a known decorator rather than applying an arbitrary callable to a class object.

not_proven.category: stacked class decorators and decorator ordering
not_proven.reason: Not exercised by this fixture.

proven.category: non-ASCII identifiers in the Latin-1 accented range (`café`, `naïve`)

not_proven.category: identifiers in non-Latin scripts (Greek, Cyrillic, CJK)
not_proven.reason: The fixture uses only accented Latin letters.

not_proven.category: NFKC normalization of identifiers
not_proven.reason: PEP 3131 requires identifiers to be normalized to NFKC; no fixture compares two differently-composed spellings of the same identifier.

proven.category: zero-argument `super().__init__()` in a subclass constructor
zero-argument `super().method()` calls through a three-level hierarchy
`super().<property>` calling the base class's getter rather than a subclass override
`super().<class attribute>` reading the base class's value, including an earlier MRO entry's class attribute outranking a later entry's same-named `@property`

not_proven.category: `super().<instance attribute>` raising `AttributeError`
not_proven.reason: pycc rejects `super().<instance attribute>` at compile time with `T0047` (#587), matching CPython's refusal to resolve it, so no fixture can exercise CPython's runtime `AttributeError` against a binary that never builds. The class-level half a `super` object does proxy is proven above.

not_proven.category: explicit two-argument `super(C, self)`
not_proven.reason: Only the zero-argument form this row names is exercised.

rows.feature: `raise ... from ...` cause chaining and `from None` suppression (#382, #540)

proven.category: `raise X from Y` inside a handler raising `X` and reaching an enclosing handler for `X`
`raise X from None` inside a handler behaving identically to a plain `raise X` for control flow
the whole `from`-clause form compiling and running in both `--debug` and `--release`

not_proven.category: `__cause__` being observable on the raised exception
not_proven.reason: pycc materializes no exception object with attributes, so the cause the `from` clause records cannot be read back. The PEP's whole point is unobservable until then.

not_proven.category: `__suppress_context__` distinguishing `from None` from a plain `raise`
not_proven.reason: `from None` currently lowers to the same HIR as a plain `raise`; the distinction has to be reintroduced when implicit `__context__` chaining lands. Tracked by #606.

not_proven.category: traceback output showing `The above exception was the direct cause of ...` or its suppression
not_proven.reason: #707 made pycc's `exception_print_and_exit` walk the `.cause` chain and print CPython's exact `The above exception was the direct cause of the following exception:` separator between an uncaught exception's own `Traceback` block and its cause's (unit-tested directly in `pycc_rt::exception`'s `render_exception_chain`). What remains unproven here is CPython-diff evidence, not the rendering itself: this repository's conformance oracle (`tests/conformance.rs`) only diffs the stdout of a *successful* run, and an uncaught `raise ... from ...` always exits 1, so there is no automated byte-for-byte comparison of this stderr text against CPython's own (which also carries file/line info pycc's frames do not -- see the PEP 3110 row's matching not-proven entry). Not #606's scope, which is exclusively about implicit `__context__` (the citation here predated #707).

proven.category: the `u''` string-literal prefix accepted and evaluated as `str`

not_proven.category: prefix combinations such as `ur''`
not_proven.reason: PEP 414 restored only the bare `u` prefix. Python 3 rejects every combination of `u` with `r`, `b`, or `f` as a syntax error, so there is no valid combined-prefix category for a fixture to cover.

not_proven.reason: The fixture prints `.value` and `.name` rather than the members themselves.

not_proven.reason: Recorded in #248 as a documented boundary.

not_proven.reason: Recorded in #248 as a documented boundary.

not_proven.category: callable and generic type forms beyond the builtin generics rows
not_proven.reason: Recorded in #248 as a documented boundary.

not_proven.category: format specifiers (`{value:.1f}`)
not_proven.reason: Rejected with C0001 at crates/pycc_hir/src/expr.rs:487.

not_proven.category: conversion flags (`!r`, `!s`, `!a`)
not_proven.reason: Rejected with C0001 at crates/pycc_hir/src/expr.rs:481.

proven.category: underscore grouping in a decimal integer literal (`1_000_000`)

not_proven.category: underscores in float, hex, octal, and binary literals
not_proven.reason: Only the decimal integer form is exercised.

not_proven.category: rejection of malformed groupings (`1__0`, `_1`, `1_`)
not_proven.reason: The PEP's negative half has no diagnostics fixture bound to this row.

proven.category: raising and catching FileNotFoundError and TimeoutError by their own exact type, and raising OSError directly and catching it by its own exact type

raising BrokenPipeError (a ConnectionError grandchild) and catching it via a handler naming ConnectionError, and separately via a handler naming the OSError root, without ever naming BrokenPipeError itself
a sibling handler not catching an unrelated family member, across several except clauses on one try
finally running on the exceptional path through this hierarchy

not_proven.category: errno-based construction/dispatch and the errno/filename/strerror/winerror instance attributes
not_proven.reason: Explicitly out of scope for #739 (Part 2 of #543), blocked on Part 3 of #541 and tracked by https://github.com/rotnov/pycc/issues/703; the fixture's registration comment in tests/conformance.rs records this and the fixture itself does not exercise any of those attributes.

not_proven.category: 9 of the 11 direct OSError subclasses are never individually raised and caught by their own exact type (BlockingIOError, ChildProcessError, ConnectionError, FileExistsError, InterruptedError, IsADirectoryError, NotADirectoryError, PermissionError, ProcessLookupError), and 3 of ConnectionError's 4 further subclasses are entirely untouched (ConnectionAbortedError, ConnectionRefusedError, ConnectionResetError)
not_proven.reason: pep_3151_oserror.py exercises a representative slice of the 16-class hierarchy -- FileNotFoundError and TimeoutError individually by exact type, BrokenPipeError only as a handler-caught superclass instance, ConnectionError and OSError as handler types -- rather than every class byte-for-byte against the CPython oracle. The remaining classes are defined as HirClassDefs (#739) but not exercised by this fixture at all.

proven.category: annotated assignment with an initializer (`doubled: int = ...`)
a bare annotation without an initializer (`total: int`)

not_proven.category: parenthesized annotated targets (`(x): int = 1`)
not_proven.reason: Rejected with C0001 at crates/pycc_hir/src/stmt.rs:195; CPython accepts it with distinct annotation-recording semantics.

not_proven.reason: pycc has no runtime annotation mapping.

not_proven.category: annotated attribute and subscript targets (`obj.x: int`, `d['k']: int`)
not_proven.reason: Not exercised by this fixture.

synthesized `__eq__` across equal and unequal instances
synthesized `__repr__`
`ClassVar` members excluded from the synthesized `__init__`, `__eq__`, and `__repr__`

not_proven.reason: Field defaults are rejected with C0001 (see crates/pycc_hir/src/class.rs) and deferred to a follow-up issue.

not_proven.category: `frozen=`, `order=`, `eq=`, and the other `@dataclass` parameters
not_proven.reason: Keyword arguments to the decorator are not exercised, and a decorator call is not one of the shapes Parts 1 and 2 of #884 bind keywords or defaults for.

not_proven.category: `__post_init__` and `InitVar`
not_proven.reason: Not exercised by this fixture.

Remove this entry (and flip PYTHON_STANDARDS.md's row) once that run is recorded.

a key inserted after construction appended at the end

`@runtime_checkable` applied to the protocol

reading a `Final` constant from a function body

not_proven.reason: The PEP's entire enforcement purpose is a negative behavior with no diagnostics fixture bound to this row.

not_proven.reason: PEP 591's `@final` decorator half is not exercised.

not_proven.category: bare `Final` without a subscript

rows.feature: Builtin generics: `list[int]` (D-105), `dict[str, int]`/`set[int]` (D-121/D-122, PR-11a), and `tuple[...]` (D-115/D-116, PR-11b) all ship real codegen, and since D-228 (issue #918), widened by issue #925, the parameterized *annotation* forms `list[T]`, `set[T]`, `dict[K, V]` and `tuple[A, B, ...]` are lowered — joined by `frozenset[T]` since #1326 (Part 1 of #1319), with `frozenset()`/`frozenset(x)` construction from a `set[int]`, `frozenset[int]` or `list[int]` — in parameter, return, local- and module-variable and type-alias positions, with explicit arity validation (`T0053`) and the same element-type capability gates the literals run (`T0034`/`T0036`/`T0038`/`T0039`). Passing a container *value* across a function boundary now works from real Python source in both directions — an annotated parameter (#918) and an annotated return type (#925) — measured end to end for all five families against CPython 3.14 (`frozenset[int]`: `tests/issue_1326_frozenset.rs`). Still deferred: a **protocol attribute's** type (not supported yet; a protocol *method's* parameter and return type both lower), a container-typed instance attribute other than a `list[int]`/`dict[str, int]` seeded from an `__init__` parameter (that case shipped in #1262), nested containers (#895), unions inside containers (#747), `type[...]` (no `Ty` variant; the D-109 16-byte ceiling is not the obstacle, as `frozenset[T]`'s measurement showed), the variadic `tuple[int, ...]` and empty `tuple[()]` (both rejected with `T0053`), and inferring an empty literal's element type from its annotation (#927)

`dict[str, int]` construction, subscript, update, and iteration
`set[int]` literal construction with `len` and duplicate elimination

not_proven.category: `frozenset[...]`, `type[...]`, and the remaining builtin generic aliases
not_proven.reason: Not exercised by a conformance fixture. `frozenset[int]` ships (#1326) and is proven against CPython by `tests/issue_1326_frozenset.rs`; `type[...]` has no `Ty` variant.

not_proven.reason: Only a single string metadata element is exercised.

not_proven.reason: Only an `int` alias is exercised.

not_proven.category: non-scalar interpolation operands (`list`/`dict`/`set`/`tuple` values)
not_proven.reason: pycc's codegen converts an interpolation operand through the shared `to_str` helper (crates/pycc_codegen/src/lib.rs), which handles only `Str`/`Int`/`Float`/`Bool` scalars and panics on `List`/`Dict`/`Tuple` (a `set`/`frozenset` operand is refused earlier as `C0001`) because v0.2 defines no `str(list)`/`str(dict)`/`str(set)` semantics (D-105/D-123/D-124); PEP 701's grammar changes therefore cannot be observed over those operand types.

rows.feature: Comprehension inlining semantics -- pycc has no bytecode/frame model to "inline" the way CPython's own PEP 709 change does; this row instead verifies the one CPython-observable, statically-testable guarantee PEP 709 depends on: a comprehension's own loop variable does not leak into an enclosing same-named binding (D-117/D-120)

proven.category: a list comprehension's iteration variable not leaking into the enclosing scope
the comprehension's produced elements

not_proven.category: the inlining itself
not_proven.reason: PEP 709's observable contract is that comprehension inlining is not detectable from Python semantics; pycc has no bytecode or frame model, so there is no surface on which the inlining itself could be proven or violated. This is a permanent non-goal, not an unimplemented category.

not_proven.category: dict and set comprehensions, and nested comprehensions
not_proven.reason: Only a single-clause list comprehension is exercised, and multi-`for`/multi-`if` comprehensions are rejected with C0001.

proven.category: a surviving stdlib module (`math`) importable with function and constant access
a removed stdlib module (`cgi`) rejected at import

not_proven.category: the other modules PEP 594 removed
not_proven.reason: PEP 594 removes stdlib modules. pycc_std implements an explicitly allowlisted subset per docs/STDLIB_PLAN.md, so every module outside that allowlist is unavailable by construction rather than by a removal pass. There is no per-module category left to implement.

rows.feature: **Deferred annotations** — pycc reads annotations exactly per 3.14 semantics; self-referential class-name annotations in own methods work (#387 Part 2)

proven.category: a class name used as an annotation inside its own body before the class is complete
methods typed by the enclosing class and dispatched at runtime

not_proven.category: `annotationlib` and the lazy-evaluation format selectors PEP 749 defines
not_proven.reason: `annotationlib` is a stdlib surface tracked by docs/STDLIB_PLAN.md, not a language semantics category. PEP 649/749's language-level contract -- that annotations are not evaluated eagerly -- is separate from the library API that inspects them.

not_proven.category: annotations that are only valid lazily (referencing a later-defined name)
not_proven.reason: Only self-reference within the class body is exercised.

proven.category: bare-comma except A, B: catching each of two named types, alongside the pre-existing parenthesized except (A, B): form
an as binding (parenthesized form) whose bound value is re-raised and recaught by an outer handler
a 3+-type handler (parenthesized form) and a non-matching raise propagating through an inner handler to an outer one

not_proven.category: a 3+-type handler written with the bare-comma spelling (only the parenthesized (A, B, C): form is exercised)
not_proven.reason: pep_0758_except_noparens.py's three_type_handler_catches_key_error test uses the parenthesized form; no fixture exercises except A, B, C: (bare comma, 3+ types) against the CPython oracle.

not_proven.category: except A, B as e: (bare comma combined with an as binding)
not_proven.reason: CPython's own grammar requires parentheses around a multi-type except handler whenever it also binds a name -- tests/diagnostics_test.rs:96-100 (l0001_except_multi_type_as_binding_requires_parens) records this as existing, already-correct parser behavior verified against the CPython oracle, not a pycc capability gap. Rejecting this shape with L0001 matches CPython; there is no valid CPython program in this category left unexercised. Only the parenthesized except (A, B) as e: form is valid Python and it is exercised.

not_proven.category: unparenthesized except* A, B: (PEP 758's own title covers both except and except* without parentheses; this row's fixture and D-195's implementation address only plain except)
not_proven.reason: Part 3 of #382 (#542, PEP 654) has since added except* itself, including the bare-comma multi-type spelling (except* A, B: parses and dispatches the same way except A, B: does, reusing D-195's own per-handler multi-tag machinery) -- but no fixture in this suite exercises that combination against the CPython oracle yet, so it stays an unproven gap on this row rather than the still-unimplemented one recorded here previously.

proven.category: a walrus inside an `if` condition, with the bound name read both inside the branch and afterward at module scope
a walrus inside a `while` condition, the classic read-until-sentinel shape
a walrus as a bare expression statement
a walrus nested inside a larger expression -- a function call argument and an arithmetic operand, including two walruses chained inside one expression
a walrus inside a function body, with the bound name visible to later statements in the same function scope

not_proven.category: a walrus value of any type other than int/float/bool/None (including Optional of those)
not_proven.reason: New diagnostic T0050 (added by PR #787) restricts a walrus value to int/float/bool/None because codegen's NamedExpr-yielding read is only worked out for those types' refcount contract; extending it to every reference-counted type was PR #787's own deliberate scope cut, recorded in its PR body and the fixture's own header comment.

not_proven.category: a walrus target nested inside a comprehension
not_proven.reason: CPython binds a walrus target to the nearest enclosing function or module scope, skipping comprehension scopes -- #774's own Scope section recorded this as an acceptable scope cut if pycc's comprehension lowering does not yet model nested scopes precisely, and PR #787's body confirms it was taken: comprehension-scope walrus is out of scope, matching CPython's own comprehension-scope-skip semantics, a D-177 core gap.

proven.category: a single `except*` clause catching a raised exception of matching type
multiple `except*` clauses on the same `try`, dispatching to the one matching the raised type
an `ExceptionGroup` constructed from multiple caught exceptions of different types, split across multiple `except*` clauses by member type
`except* ... as` binding capturing the resulting (matched) `ExceptionGroup`
`except*`/`finally` interaction -- the `finally` block still runs
`except*`/`else` interaction -- the `else` block runs when the `try` body raises nothing

not_proven.category: `ExceptionGroup.subgroup(condition)` and `ExceptionGroup.split(condition)`
not_proven.reason: Neither method is implemented yet; tracked by #775 as an independent follow-up to #542, since they are independently testable without further except* matching machinery.

not_proven.category: an `except*` clause body containing a direct `return`, `break`, or `continue`
not_proven.reason: Rejected as intended since #795: HIR lowering reports L0001 ("'return' in an 'except*' block", and likewise for `break`/`continue`), matching CPython's own `SyntaxError: 'break', 'continue' and 'return' cannot appear in an except* block`. A loop entered within the clause body shields `break`/`continue` but not `return`, and a module-level `return` still reports the pre-existing T0024 -- both verified against CPython 3.14.6. Not provable by the conformance fixture, which must be valid Python the pinned oracle can run; the behaviour is pinned by the public-CLI diagnostic fixtures tests/diagnostics/l0001_return_in_except_star.py, l0001_return_in_loop_in_except_star.py, l0001_break_in_except_star.py, l0001_continue_in_except_star.py, l0001_break_in_except_star_inside_loop.py, l0001_break_in_except_star_in_finally.py, and d0024_return_in_except_star_at_module_level.py, so this is out-of-scope rather than a core gap -- the same basis as rule 11's `except A, B as e:` entry.

not_proven.category: `except* ExceptionGroup:`, `except* BaseExceptionGroup:`, and an `except*` handler naming a user class derived from either group type
not_proven.reason: CPython accepts both names at compile time and raises TypeError ("catching ExceptionGroup with except* is not allowed. Use except instead.") at handler-match time. The same TypeError fires for a user subclass (class G(ExceptionGroup)) as for the group class itself. Since #795, pycc rejects all of them at compile time with C0001 instead -- a deliberate divergence recorded in D-223 (which narrows D-202), because D-173 propagates a raised exception through global runtime state rather than a materialized group instance, so there is no value to type-test at match time and no mechanism for raising a TypeError from generated except* dispatch. Still a core gap: the observable behaviour differs from CPython's. Tracked by #903; the compile-time rejection is pinned by tests/diagnostics/c0001_except_star_exception_group.py, c0001_except_star_base_exception_group_in_tuple.py, and c0001_except_star_exception_group_subclass.py.

not_proven.category: D-202's six deliberate simplifications (ExceptionGroup identity through subgroup/split reconstruction, restrictions on dynamic non-literal member lists, and related narrowings)
not_proven.reason: D-202 itself records each simplification as independently revisitable once a materialized exception instance (#703) and/or a genuinely dynamic group object become available -- not a permanent non-goal, so D-177 does not permit classifying it `out-of-scope`. Each is enforced by its own diagnostic or fixed reconstructed identity today rather than an unimplemented capability, but the underlying infrastructure gap (no dynamic group object, no materialized instance identity) is real, unimplemented core work.

proven.category: `from __future__ import annotations` accepted as the module's first statement after the leading comment block, compiling as a no-op

the directive accepted alongside a method parameter annotated with its own enclosing class (`other: Node` inside `class Node`) -- the same shape the PEP 649/749 row proves, shown here to be unaffected by the no-op directive
module-level function parameters and return annotated with an already-defined class and `int`, called and printed byte-identically
a string annotation naming the enclosing class (`def clone(self) -> "Node"`), resolved exactly like its unquoted spelling (Part 1 of #889)

not_proven.category: a forward reference to a name defined *later* in the module, quoted or not (PEP 563's distinguishing case)
not_proven.reason: Not exercised by the fixture because pycc rejects it today with `C0001: type annotation ... is not supported yet`; the directive is accepted as a no-op (D-229) but annotation resolution is still eager, so the later-defined name is unresolved at the annotation site. Quoting it does not help: a string annotation resolves exactly like its unquoted spelling, and resolving a later-defined class is deferred on #889.

not_proven.category: `__annotations__` introspection (the stringified annotation values the directive produces)
not_proven.reason: Not exercised by the fixture and not implemented: pycc has no runtime `__annotations__` object on functions, classes, or modules, so the directive's observable effect on introspection (stringified values) cannot be compared against the oracle. D-164 rejected runtime introspection only as the mechanism for dataclass field discovery, which reads annotations statically instead; it did not declare a runtime annotation object a permanent non-goal, so under D-177 this stays `core` rather than `out-of-scope`.

not_proven.category: feature-name binding: reading `annotations` after the import (CPython binds it to a `__future__._Feature` object)
not_proven.reason: Deliberate divergence recorded by D-229: pycc binds nothing, so a later read of `annotations` is `T0021` where CPython prints the feature object. The fixture never reads the name, so the directive is proven only as an accepted no-op for this program, not as a binding-equivalent import.
